transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Recording: fireflies.ai
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Redwood CSM), Ravi Singh (Proxima Head of Security), Marta Kovac (CTO), Leo Park (Platform), Sara O'Neill (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Review of recent penetration test findings and remediation status; discussion of vulnerability management and patch cadence.
- Questions about KMS integration, data residency for EU customers, and audit log retention.
- Agreement to exchange redacted pen-test PDF and run Redwood vulnerability harness against Proxima staging.

Topics: pen test overview; vulnerability triage & SLA; secure SDLC practices; patch cadence and maintenance windows; RBAC/SSO and audit logging; KMS/encryption; SOC 2 evidence handoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ravi Singh: Hey, Ravi here.
[00:08] Marta Kovac: Marta, hi.
[00:09] Leo Park: Leo, Platform.
[00:11] Sara O'Neill: Sara, compliance.
[00:14] Diego Marquez: Diego from Redwood infra team.
[00:16] Anika Patel: Anika, CSM.
[00:18] Laura Chen: Cool. We're here to walk through the pen-test results, how you triaged them, and align on patch cadence and SDLC improvements. Diego will drive the vuln/patch section.

[00:45] Diego Marquez: Ok, quick context: we saw the report you shared last week — thanks for the redacted copy — it was the external network and app level pen test, right?
[00:51] Ravi Singh: Correct, external + authenticated app tests. There were some medium-high findings mostly around outdated libraries and a couple of config issues on the kube clusters.
[01:12] Diego Marquez: Got it. When you say kube clusters, is that our managed infra or customer-managed? (note: transcription sometimes shows "cube")
[01:20] Ravi Singh: It's our infra; our platform team manages clusters but we run some customer workloads in their VPC via the private deployment.

[01:34] Marta Kovac: I want to clarify: the report flagged a couple of CVEs in the model-serving stack — one was a dependency in the transformer tokenizer, and another was in the HTTP proxy.
[01:46] Diego Marquez: That aligns. We actually see those in other customers too; many are dependency chain issues. Two tracks for remediation: immediate patch + compensating controls (WAF, network rules), and medium-term upgrade in the build pipeline.

[02:10] Leo Park: Our main ask is the patch cadence. We can't do weekly forced restarts for production. Typical window we have is monthly maintenance, but we can do emergency patches.
[02:22] Laura Chen: That's totally reasonable. What patch SLA does Proxima target today?
[02:27] Ravi Singh: For high severity we aim for 72 hours for critical, 14 days for high, 30–60 days for medium. But honestly, we missed a couple because of scheduling and regression fear.

[02:46] Diego Marquez: On Redwood side, we recommend a combined approach: allow scheduled monthly non-prod upgrades, and for critical CVEs we have an emergency rollback-safe path. We can help automate canary rollouts and patch testing — Diego explains the canary harness.

[03:10] Diego Marquez: (explaining) Our canary process snapshots the model container and runs a smoke/e2e against a small traffic slice. We also keep KV cache state isolated so it doesn't bleed into main traffic. Note — sometimes transcriber shows K V cash or K-V cache as "cash" so apologies.

[03:45] Sara O'Neill: On the compliance side, the report asked for evidence: do you have a software SBOM and dependency tracking for model-serving images?
[03:54] Anika Patel: We have SBOM exports from the build system. I'll share the artifact link after the call; it's been used for SOC2 audits previously.

[04:10] Marta Kovac: How does Redwood handle key management? The pen-test flagged key rotation gaps — KMS integration and HSM-backed keys.
[04:20] Diego Marquez: We support external KMS — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault — and we can do bring-your-own-key via our private deployment. Rotation policies are configurable; we also support HSM via PKCS#11 in on-prem. Occasionally the transcript may read K-M-S as spelled out which is just the speech engine.

[04:49] Ravi Singh: For data residency, EU customers require keys to stay in region. Can Redwood guarantee no key material leaves region in the private deployment?
[04:58] Laura Chen: For private deployments yes — keys remain customer-controlled in their KMS. For hosted we have region controls and can use customer-managed keys with regional endpoints. We'll share the region/KMS mapping doc.

[05:20] Leo Park: Back to vuln management: do you provide a vulnerability feed or CVE alerts for customers?
[05:25] Diego Marquez: Yes, we push security advisories for platform deps and curated model vulnerabilities. We also integrate with client slack/webhooks for high sev alerts.

[05:40] Ravi Singh: The pen-test authors also requested audit log retention details. What's default retention for request/response logs vs metadata?
[05:48] Anika Patel: By default hosted logs are retained 90 days at request level; metadata and traces 365 days. In Dedicated/Private we can configure retention to match customer policy and export to SIEM.

[06:10] Marta Kovac: Do logs contain PII or model outputs? We need to know the sensitive fields redaction policy.
[06:16] Diego Marquez: We redact customer-specified fields by default and have structured logging knobs for PII patterns. For private deployments you can disable collection of full outputs entirely — we can also route logs directly to your SIEM.

[06:40] Ravi Singh: On the pen-test specifics: one medium finding was an HTTP header misconfiguration allowing X-Frame options missing on one proxy. Has that been patched?
[06:48] Laura Chen: Our engineering team pushed a config change last week; I believe it's fixed in latest staging. Diego, can you confirm?

[06:55] Diego Marquez: Confirmed — patched in staging; scheduled to roll to prod in next maintenance window. We'll add that to the remediation tracker. (Note: tracker link shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/pen-test/proxima/tracker )

[07:20] Sara O'Neill: About secure SDLC: the pen-test recommended a dependency upgrade gating step in CI. Do you support SBOM-based gating?
[07:28] Diego Marquez: Yes, we have a CI step that fails builds on policy violations, and you can gate on SBOM vulnerabilities threshold. We can share a sample policy.

[07:45] Marta Kovac: Do you run fuzzing or mutate test harnesses on model endpoints? That's something our infra team likes to run.
[07:54] Diego Marquez: We run targeted fuzz tests for protocol parsers and open-source servables; for model-level adversarial testing, we provide a test harness customers can run locally. We don't fuzz customer prompts in production.

[08:20] Laura Chen: Let's talk RBAC and SSO — the report said service accounts had excessive privileges. How granular are permissions?
[08:28] Diego Marquez: Our RBAC model supports roles and resource-level permissions. For private deployments you can map to your IAM via OIDC/SAML. We recommend least-privilege and short-lived tokens; the platform supports session expiry and automatic token rotation.

[08:49] Ravi Singh: Are there logs for service account usage? We need to map any suspicious activity to identity.
[08:55] Anika Patel: Yes — every API key/service token call is logged with actor metadata and request signature; we can export to your SIEM with user mapping.

[09:15] Leo Park: Another item in the pen-test was a stale container image in one of our test clusters. How do you recommend ensuring images in registries are pruned and updated?
[09:24] Diego Marquez: We recommend immutable tags, automated image scanning on push, and GC policies. The Redwood CI can auto-bump base images and open PRs when vulnerabilities are found.

[09:50] Marta Kovac: On model outputs, the pen-test had a note about model theft risk if endpoints are overly permissive. What rate-limiting and throttling controls exist?
[09:59] Diego Marquez: We provide per-route rate limits, token-based quotas, and content-length caps. For sensitive models we can enable stricter rate limits and anomaly detection to block exfil patterns.

[10:20] Ravi Singh: Can you proactively scan model weights for watermarking or fingerprinting evidence?
[10:26] Diego Marquez: We don't scan model weights for IP fingerprinting ourselves, that's usually part of customer IP protection tooling. We can integrate with third-party detection or include hooks for offline analysis.

[10:45] Laura Chen: Quick check — any blockers from our side to move forward with remediation?
[10:50] Ravi Singh: We need the redacted pen-test in full, the SBOM export, and a list of the remediation resources you propose. Then we'll commit to a patch schedule.

[11:05] Diego Marquez: We'll prepare a remediation plan mapping each finding to a fix, compensating controls, owner, and ETA. We'll also run our vuln harness against your staging cluster to validate.

[11:25] Marta Kovac: On the SOC 2 angle — we need evidence for change control and patch history. Can you provide change logs and deploy audit trails?
[11:33] Anika Patel: Yes, we can provide deploy audit trails and immutable change logs for dedicated/private. For hosted we can provide consolidated artifacts; for enterprise we have SOC 2 evidence bundles.

[11:50] Ravi Singh: One nuance: the pen test flagged lack of proof-of-rotation for a specific key — not the KMS functionality but the rotation logs were missing. Can you surface rotation events?
[11:59] Diego Marquez: Rotation events are logged — we'll double-check retention settings. Might be that short retention on the test environment dropped older events. We can increase retention or export to your audit store.

[12:20] Laura Chen: Let's spend a few minutes on prioritization — which findings are highest priority from your viewpoint?
[12:27] Ravi Singh: From our internal risk scoring: the tokenizer CVE (RCE risk) is high, the HTTP proxy header config is medium, and some infra misconfigs are medium.

[12:43] Diego Marquez: We'll mark RCE/tokenizer as P0 and propose an immediate patch + canary validation. For medium items we'll bundle into the next monthly maintenance window.

[13:05] Marta Kovac: About patch testing — Leo, do you have test coverage for model-serving edge cases?
[13:11] Leo Park: We have smoke and e2e, but not exhaustive fuzzing. We'll work with Redwood test harness to expand coverage.

[13:28] Laura Chen: Good. I also want to note an operational control: we can enable automatic fallback to a verified model variant if a canary fails, to reduce impact.

[13:45] Diego Marquez: Yes, automatic fallback + circuit breaker on token spikes.

[14:00] Ravi Singh: A question about encryption in transit: the pen-test referenced deprecated TLS ciphers on one internal proxy. Is that part of the managed layer?
[14:09] Diego Marquez: It's configurable. We default to modern TLS profiles but older test clusters sometimes have legacy configs. We'll push the TLS profile update and validate with SSL scanners.

[14:35] Sara O'Neill: For auditability, do you provide signed audit logs or append-only storage?
[14:42] Diego Marquez: We can provide append-only backed by object store immutability and optionally sign logs with customer KMS keys.

[15:00] Laura Chen: Anything else on the pen-test?
[15:03] Ravi Singh: One oddity — the pen-test noted excessive privileges on a prod DB read role used by a monitoring agent. We disabled that agent this morning but need guidance on least privilege.

[15:15] Diego Marquez: Recommend creating a dedicated read-only role with column-level restrictions and short-lived credentials. Use service account rotation and map to RBAC rules.

[15:34] Marta Kovac: On SSO — we've had some flakey SAML assertions failing for user provisioning. Is that something Redwood has visibility into?
[15:41] Anika Patel: We log SAML success/fail events and can share the SAML debug logs. We'll need the assertion IDs to trace specific failures.

[16:00] Leo Park: Regarding deployment guarantees, if we patch a model-serving image, will sessions be preserved or will clients observe errors?
[16:09] Diego Marquez: With session affinity and graceful shutdown hooks we drain in-flight requests; clients might see short latency blips but not hard failures. We test drain behavior on canaries.

[16:30] Ravi Singh: We also need a timeline for rolling back if a patch regresses.
[16:35] Diego Marquez: Rollbacks are supported and we keep previous stable container images; we can automate rollback on regression detection in the canary harness.

[17:00] Laura Chen: Ok let's pivot to the secure SDLC notes — code review, dependency gating, CI SBOM policy, and PR workflows.

[17:14] Diego Marquez: Our recommended SDLC: SBOM on build, auto-scan for known CVEs, gated PRs for infra changes, and reproducible builds. Also we suggest a periodic dependency upgrade cadence — e.g., biweekly staged updates.

[17:40] Marta Kovac: Biweekly upgrades sound aggressive for us; can we instead do monthly upgrades but with auto PRs and policy tests?
[17:47] Diego Marquez: Absolutely — monthly is common. The key is to have automated tests and canaries so that monthly updates can still be low-risk.

[18:05] Ravi Singh: A small ask — can Redwood share a sample policy file for SBOM gating so we can test in our CI?
[18:11] Laura Chen: We'll send the sample policy and a short README.

[18:25] Sara O'Neill: On retention and evidence for SOC 2, we'll need ISO docs and the latest SOC 2 Type II report.
[18:32] Anika Patel: I have a link to the SOC 2 evidence portal — Laura will share. For ISO we'll include cert numbers and auditor contact.

[18:50] Marta Kovac: For patch cadences, let's get concrete: Ravi, what do you propose?
[18:55] Ravi Singh: P0: 72 hours; P1: 14 days; P2: 45 days. We'll adopt Redwood's canary for P0s. For P1/P2 we'll schedule in the monthly window and have a backstop for emergency fixes.

[19:18] Diego Marquez: Sounds good. We'll mirror that SLA in our remediation tracker so owners can be assigned.

[19:40] Laura Chen: Any concerns about data residency with these remediation steps?
[19:45] Marta Kovac: None if logs and keys remain in-region.

[19:52] Laura Chen: Good. A couple of practical items: we'll attach the tracker link and pen-test redacted PDF to the CRM and share the follow-up calendar invite for the remediation sync.

[20:08] Ravi Singh: One more note — the pen-test vendor suggested additional dynamic scanning on model endpoints to measure prompt injection vectors. We'll likely ask Redwood for tooling recommendations.

[20:22] Diego Marquez: We have a prompt-security checklist and some recommended third-party tools; we'll send those links.

[20:38] Marta Kovac: Will Redwood's observability show model-level latencies per route so we can detect anomalies that might indicate exfil attempts?
[20:45] Diego Marquez: Yes, per-route token and latency metrics, and anomaly detection hooks with alerting.

[21:05] Laura Chen: Ok let's pause for any outstanding questions from Proxima.

[21:12] Sara O'Neill: Are there documented SLAs for audit log exports? We need to show auditors.
[21:18] Anika Patel: Yes, export SLAs are in the enterprise packet; I'll attach the specific page.

[21:34] Leo Park: Regarding private deployment, what does the upgrade path look like? Do you push code or do we pull?
[21:40] Diego Marquez: For private we provide deployment bundles and scripts; you can pull and control timing, or we can assist via runbooks if you want a managed upgrade.

[21:55] Ravi Singh: One compliance question: do you support customer-managed encryption-at-rest keys with regional constraints for EU?
[22:02] Laura Chen: Yes — bring-your-own-key in-region is supported in private, and hosted customers can supply CMKs scoped to regions. We'll share the constraints doc.

[22:20] Marta Kovac: Ok that's helpful. Anything else on SOC 2/ISO?

[22:25] Anika Patel: We'll compile an evidence bundle: SOC 2 report, ISO cert, SBOM exports, rotation logs, deploy audit logs. Expect that by 2025-05-09.

[22:40] Diego Marquez: We'll also run the Redwood vuln harness against the Proxima staging cluster; plan to share the scan report.

[23:00] Ravi Singh: On remediation owners — we want names assigned per finding.

[23:06] Laura Chen: We'll do that in the tracker; Diego will propose owners and you can reassign.

[23:20] Marta Kovac: Quick question on scanning frequency — how often do you scan managed images?

[23:25] Diego Marquez: We scan nightly for critical advisories and weekly for broad scans; we can increase cadence for customers during remediation windows.

[23:45] Leo Park: For our internal SDLC adjustments, we'll need sample PR templates to include SBOM and security checklist.

[23:52] Laura Chen: We'll include those in the follow-up package.

[24:08] Ravi Singh: A procedural question: once remediation is done, does Redwood provide attestations?

[24:14] Anika Patel: Yes, we can provide remediation attestations and validation reports for closed findings.

[24:30] Marta Kovac: For the patch schedule, can we have a 48-hour freeze window notification so our on-call can be prepared?

[24:36] Diego Marquez: Yes — we can configure automated alerts 48/24/1 hour pre-maintenance.

[24:50] Laura Chen: Great. I'm going to summarize next steps now.

[24:55] Laura Chen: Redwood will: 1) share redacted full pen-test PDF and remediation tracker by 2025-05-09; 2) run vuln harness against staging and share scan by 2025-05-14; 3) send SOC2/ISO evidence bundle by 2025-05-09; 4) provide SBOM policy sample and CI gating example.

[25:20] Ravi Singh: Proxima will: 1) provide prioritized CVE list and confirm patch windows by 2025-05-12; 2) enable temporary access to staging for the vuln harness; 3) review remediation owners and confirm.

[25:38] Diego Marquez: I'll assign owners in the tracker and ping maintainers.

[25:45] Marta Kovac: One last question: in the event of an exploited CVE, what's the notification SLA?

[25:52] Laura Chen: For critical incidents we have a 30-minute initial notification SLA and a dedicated incident channel. We'll include that in the runbook.

[26:10] Ravi Singh: Thanks, that's important.

[26:15] Laura Chen: Any other items?

[26:18] Sara O'Neill: Nothing from compliance side.
[26:20] Leo Park: All good.

[26:25] Laura Chen: Ok, we'll wrap. I'll send the follow-up with attachments and calendar invite for the remediation sync. Thanks everyone.

[26:34] Meeting end (transcribed until ~26 minutes; call remained for a short private post-call convo).

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and minor word swaps (e.g., KV cache -> K-V cash). Links shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/pen-test/proxima/tracker ; SOC2 portal link (redwood-sec.example.com/soc2/proxima)
